ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Dry mouth

A patient using ipratropium reports a dry mouth after inhalations but has no swelling, rash or respiratory deterioration. Which pharmacologic action most directly explains this common local anticholinergic effect of the medication?

  1. Reduced muscarinic stimulation of salivary secretion
  2. Increased parasympathetic salivary signaling
  3. Direct activation of salivary beta-2 receptors
  4. Histamine release causing anaphylaxis in every user
  5. Inhibition of all renal water reabsorption
Answer and explanation

Reduced muscarinic stimulation of salivary secretion

Muscarinic blockade reduces glandular secretion.

Option explanations

Reduced muscarinic stimulation of salivary secretion: Muscarinic blockade reduces glandular secretion.

Increased parasympathetic salivary signaling: This would increase secretion.

Direct activation of salivary beta-2 receptors: This is not ipratropium’s action.

Histamine release causing anaphylaxis in every user: Dry mouth alone does not establish anaphylaxis.

Inhibition of all renal water reabsorption: That would not directly explain the local antimuscarinic effect.
